A general culture center where limited time events often take place. It has a library, movie theater and concerts. It is a common place for informal street dance and board game gatherings.

Constructed by and home to a wealthy Syrian family in the 1900s, this mansion later became a bank, known for its gorgeous Christmas decor. Nowadays, it's a McDonald's restaurant, with a loud and colorful look.
A public school from 1909, still fully active. It contains a neoclassical European style of architecture, in striking yellow.
A still working private hospital, built in 1906. Its outside walls contain carvings of healthcare and Catholic symbols.

Built in 1892, this small park is the most significant green area of the Paulista region. It combines features of an English garden with preserved Atlantic rainforest, plus landscaping by Roberto Burle Marx and sculptures by Clóvis Olga…
Focused on Korean culture and arts, it has a library with books, CDs and DVDs in Portuguese, Korean and English, alongside events about the country.

This pyramid-shaped building is home to the Federação das Indústrias do Estado de São Paulo, a powerful union that represents employees from over 150,000 companies, or 42% of the Brazilian GDP. It also hosts cultural expositions and…

The tallest building of the avenue contains Faculdade Cásper Líbero (a private college institution), the Gazeta radio, TV and news agency, Objetivo (a private school), Reserva Cultural (a cinema and theater) and a 95-m-high TV antenna…
An enjoyable small park to rest for a bit. It has a tourism information office and free wifi in its area, making for a good spot to plan out or review your itinerary.
Also includes a bookstore, a bistro and a French-style bakery.
Many different cuisines are represented in this street market, with unique and trendy street food from all over the world.
Small and cozy French restaurant by chef Erick Jacquin, popular in Brazil for multiple food-based reality TV shows.

Finish your museum visit here, where you can taste a unique mix of food from Bahia and Minas Gerais with international fine dining influence. The baião de dois with beef stew is a popular option, and can be finished by a banana crème…
High-end sushi spot, serves fresh oysters.
Japanese-inspired coffee shop, with trendy ingredients such as matcha. Also has Japanese-inspired snacks.
Always full on weekends, this old school bar has a privileged view of the movement of the avenue.
Cheap and fresh fruit juice, many options available.
The equivalent of Igreja da Sé for the Orthodox Antioch Church is one of the few remarkable examples of Byzantine architecture in Brazil.
Authentic Indian restaurant focused on lamb, chicken and vegetarian options.
